We consider the upper bound on this distance as an "error" of a truncated pseudo-moment sequence in the sense of how far we can move a truncated pseudo-moment sequence to a truncated moment sequence, which then delivers the tightness of the SDP relaxations within the moment hierarchy by Lemma~\ref{lemma: distance to convergence rate}. 

Because the SDP relaxations in the SOS hierarchy are the dual of the SDP relaxations in the moment sequence, for which the strong duality holds under the Archimedean condition ( see e.g., \cite{josz2016strong}), this leads to an identical convergence rate between the moment and SOS hierarchies. In addition, we construct a new certificate denoted by $\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{X})$ which is weaker than the Schmüdgen certificate, and potentially leads to a reduced version of the Schmüdgen-type hierarchy without changing the theoretical convergence rate. 

The reduction of the moment-SOS hierarchy for a real algebraic variety in \cite{S.o.S-on-real-variety} shares a similar construction, but our results provide precise convergence rates under the Archimedean condition. The connection of the error estimation of the truncated pseudo-moment sequences with the Łojasiewicz inequality directly implies the convergence rates in various special cases such as strongly convex sets, sets satisfying the Polyak-Łojasiewicz condition \eqref{def LP} or constraint qualification condition (CQC), polytopes, and spheres. In conclusion, the main results of this paper are summarized in Table~\ref{tab: results}.

nodes.statement: In this paper, we aim to determine the asymptotic convergence rate of the moment-SOS hierarchy for a compact semi-algebraic set X. Since X is bounded, there exists a constant R such that the ball B_R (with radius R and center at the origin) contains X. Without loss of generality, we can assume that R- \|x\|^2 is positive over X. The Schm\"udgen Positivstellensatz theorem implies that there exists a positive integer t such that R- \|x\|^2 in T(X)_2t. Therefore, if we set T(X')_2r to be the preordering of order 2r of X with the additional constraint R- \|x\|^2 geq 0, then we have T(X')_2rsubset T(X)_2r+2t forall\; r in N. This means that the asymptotic convergence rates of mlb(f,T(X))_r and lb(f,T(X))_r are equal to that of mlb(f,T(X'))_r and lb(f,T(X'))_r, respectively. Therefore, without loss of generality, throughout this paper, most results will be stated under the assumption that the ball constraint R^2 - \|x\|^2 geq 0 for some suitable R is added to the description~ of X.

Then the primal SDP problems in the moment hierarchies \eqref{hierarchy: moment Schmudgen},  \eqref{hierarchy: reduced moment}, and \eqref{hierarchy: moment Putinar}  can be written as the following alternatives:
\begin{align*}
    &\mathrm{mlb}(f,\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{X}))_r = \inf\left\{\sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^n_k} f_{\alpha}y_{\alpha}=\langle \mathbf{f}_k,\mathit{y} \rangle:\ \mathit{y} \in \mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{X})_{2r}) \right\},\\
    &\mathrm{mlb}(f,\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{X}))_r = \inf\left\{\sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^n_k} f_{\alpha}y_{\alpha}=\langle \mathbf{f}_k,\mathit{y} \rangle:\ \mathit{y} \in \mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{X})_{2r}) \right\},\\
    &\mathrm{mlb}(f,\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{X}))_r = \inf\left\{\sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^n_k} f_{\alpha}y_{\alpha}=\langle \mathbf{f}_k,\mathit{y} \rangle:\ \mathit{y} \in \mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{X})_{2r}) \right\},
\end{align*}
where 
\begin{eqnarray*}
\mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{X})_{2r}) &=& \{ \pi_k(y)\in \mathbb{R}^{s(n,k)} \,:\, y\in \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{X})_{2r}) \},
\\
\mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{X})_{2r}) &=& \{ \pi_k(y)\in \mathbb{R}^{s(n,k)} \,:\, y\in \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{X})_{2r}) \},
\\
\mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{X})_{2r}) &=& \{ \pi_k(y)\in \mathbb{R}^{s(n,k)} \,:\, y\in \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{X})_{2r}) \}.
\end{eqnarray*}
We have that $\mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{X})_{2r})$ and $\mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{X})_{2r})$ are outer convex approximations of $\mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{X})$, i.e.,
\begin{displaymath}
    \mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{X}) \subset \mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{X})_{2r}) \subset \mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{X})_{2r}).

\label{lemma: distance to convergence rate}

    Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a compact semi-algebraic set and $k \geq {\rm deg}(f)$. Then the errors of the $r$-level of the moment hierarchies are bounded proportionally to the Hausdorff distances as follows:
    \begin{eqnarray*}
        \qquad f_{\min} - \mathrm{mlb}(f,\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{X}))_r &\leq& \|f\|_1\,\mathbf{d}_k(\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{X})_{2r}),\\
        \qquad f_{\min} - \mathrm{mlb}(f,\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{X}))_r &\leq&\|f\|_1\,\mathbf{d}_k(\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{X})_{2r}),\\
        \qquad f_{\min} - \mathrm{mlb}(f,\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{X}))_r &\leq&\|f\|_1\,\mathbf{d}_k(\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{X})_{2r}).
    \end{eqnarray*}
    Combining with Remark~\ref{remark: Archimedian condition}, the convergence rates of the pairs of moment-SOS hierarchies \eqref{hierarchy: moment Schmudgen}--\eqref{hierarchy: SOS Schmudegen}, 
    \eqref{hierarchy: reduced moment}--\eqref{hierarchy: reduced SOS}, and 
    \eqref{hierarchy: moment Putinar}--\eqref{hierarchy: SOS Putinar} are the same as the rates of the Hausdorff distances $\mathbf{d}_k(\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{X})_{2r})$,

\label{lemma: recall results}
     Let $\mathcal{X} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be either the unit ball $B_n$ or the standard simplex $\Delta_n$  with $\mu$ as the corresponding measure listed in Table~\ref{tab:measure}. We fix $\{P_{\alpha}(\mathbf{x})\; :\; \alpha \in \mathbb{N}^n\}$ to be an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{R}[\mathbf{x}]$ with respect to the inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_{\mu}$ induced by $\mu$ on $\mathcal{X}$. Then for any $k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $r \geq 2(n+1)k$, there exists a sequence of positive numbers $\lambda = (\lambda_j)_{0 \leq j \leq 2r}$ such that
     \begin{itemize}
        \item  $\lambda_0 =1$,
         \item $C_{2r}[\mathcal{X},\mu,\lambda](\cdot,\mathbf{y}):= \sum_{j=0}^{2r}\lambda_j C^{(j)}[\mathcal{X},\mu](\cdot,\mathbf{y}) 
         \in \mathcal{T}(\mathcal{X})_{2r}\quad \forall\; \mathbf{y} \in \mathcal{X}$,
         \item $\lambda_j \in [1/2,1]\quad \forall\; 0 \leq j \leq 2r$ and\; $\sum_{j=0}^k\left|1-\dfrac{1}{\lambda_j} \right| \leq 
         \dfrac{c(n,k)}{r^2}$.
     \end{itemize}
     Here, $c(n,k) = 2(n+1)^2k^2$. In addition, the spectrum of $\mathbf{C}_{2r}[\mathcal{X},\mu,\lambda]$ consists of the eigenvalues $\lambda_j$'s for 
     $0 \leq j \leq 2r$, whose eigen-space is spanned by the set of polynomials $\{P_{\alpha}(\mathbf{x})\; :\;\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^n,\; |\alpha|= j\}$.

nodes.statement: The orthogonality of \P^(i)_alpha^(i):\ alpha^ (i) in N^n_i\ implies that for any P_alpha(x) satisfying alpha=(alpha^(1),dots,alpha^(m)) in N^n,\ |alpha^(i)|=j_i,\ sum_i=1^mj_i leq 2r, the following identities hold: &K P_alpha(x)\;=\; int_Xleft(prod_i=1^mC_2r[X_i,mu_i,lambda^(i)](x^(i),overlinex^(i))right) cdot left( prod_i=1^mP^(i)_alpha^(i)(overlinex^(i))right)dmu(overlinex)\\ =\;& prod_i=1^mleft(int_X_iC_2r[X_i,mu_i,lambda^(i)](x^(i),overlinex^(i))P^(i)_alpha^(i)(overlinex^(i) )dmu_i(overlinex^(i))right)\\ =\;& prod_i=1^m left(lambda^(i)_j_iP^(i)_alpha^(i)(x^(i)) right)= left(prod_i=1^m lambda^(i)_j_iright)P_alpha(x), and &C_2r[X,mu,lambda]P_alpha(x) =int_XC_2r[X,mu,lambda](x,overlinex) P_alpha(overlinex)dmu(overlinex)\\ =&sum_j^prime_1+dots+j^prime_mleq 2r int_X left( prod_i=1^m lambda^(i)_j_i^primeC^(j^prime_i)[X_i,mu_i](x^(i),overlinex^(i)) P^(i)_alpha^(i)(overlinex^(i)) right) dmu(overlinex) \\ =&sum_j^prime_1+dots+j_m ^primeleq 2rprod_i=1^mleft(int_X_ilambda^(i)_j_i^primeC^(j^prime_i)[X_i,mu_i] (x^(i),overlinex^(i))P^(i)_alpha^(i)(overlinex^(i))dmu_i(overlinex^(i))right)\\ =&prod_i=1^mleft(int_X_ilambda^(i)_j_iC^(j_i)[X_i,mu_i] (x^(i),overlinex^(i))P^(i)_alpha^(i)(overlinex^(i))dmu_i(overlinex^(i))right) mbox(since |alpha^(i)| = j_i) \\ =& prod_i=1^m left(lambda^(i)_j_iP^(i)_alpha^(i)(x^(i)) right)= left(prod_i=1^m lambda^(i)_j_iright)P_alpha(x). nodes.statement: For any r > 2(max\n_1,ldots,n_m\+1)k, we define K to be the linear operator on R[x]_k associated to the kernel K defined in Lemma . Since 2r geq k, Lemma~ implies that K and C_2r[X,mu,lambda] are identical on R[x]_k. Thus, it suffices to prove that the linear operator K: R[x]_k to R[x]_k satisfies , and . We recall from Lemma~ that lambda^(i)_0 =1\; forall i in [m], and 1 = prod_i=1^m P^(i)_0(x^(i)) is the eigen-polynomial of the eigenvalue prod_i=1^mlambda^(i)_0=1. This implies that K(1) = 1 mboxand hence is satisfied. We next prove by utilizing Tchakaloff's theorem (see e.g., ) to show the existence of a cubature rule for the integration of polynomials, i.e., there exist \(x_j,w_j): 1 leq j leq N := k + deg (K) \ subset X times R_>0 such that for any non-negative polynomial f in R[x]_k on X, we have that K f(x) = int_XK(x,overlinex)f(overlinex)dmu (overlinex)=sum_j=1^NK(x,x_j)w_jf(x_j). Recall that K(x,x_j)= prod_i=1^mC_2r[X_i,mu_i,lambda^(i)](x^(i),x^(i)_j). Lemma~ gives lambda^(i)'s satisfying that C_2r[X_i,mu_i,lambda^(i)](x^(i),x^(i)_j) in T(X_i)_2r forall\; i in [m],\;\; jin[N]. Therefore, K(x,x_j) = prod_i=1^mC_2r[X_i,mu_i,lambda^(i)](x^(i),x^(i)_j) in T(X)_2mr. Combining this with the condition w_jf(x_j) geq 0\ forall i in [N], we obtain property as follows: K f(x) =sum_j=1^N K(x,x_j)w_j f(x_j) in T(X)_2mr. Finally, we prove property (P3). Since lambda^(i)_j's are positive numbers, the linear operator K: R[x]_2r to R[x]_2r has all its eigenvalues being positive. Thus, the inverse K^-1 exists and the spectrum is left\left(prod_i=1^mlambda^(i)_j_iright)^-1\;:\: j_1+dots j_m leq 2r right\. Then, we have |K^-1f(x) -f(x)| &=& left|sum_j_1+dots+j_m leq kleft(1-dfrac1prod_i=1^mlambda^(i)_j_i right)f_j_1,dots,j_m(x) right| nonumber \\ &leq& left( sum_j_1dots+j_m leq kleft|1-dfrac1prod_i=1^mlambda^(i)_j_i right| right) Lambda(X,k) \|f\|_X. Taking maximum on both sides of over x in X, we obtain that \|K^-1f -f\|_X leq Lambda(X,k) \|f\|_X sum_j_1+dots+j_m leq kleft|1-dfrac1prod_i=1^mlambda^(i)_j_i right|. Based on Lemma~, we know that for all i in [m] and 0 leq j leq 2r , we have lambda^(i)_j in [1/2,1]. Then && hspace-7mm sum_j_1+dots+j_m leq kleft|1-dfrac1prod_i=1^mlambda^(i)_j_i right|= sum_j_1+dots+j_m leq kfrac1- prod_i=1^mlambda^(i)_j_iprod_i=1^mlambda^(i)_j_ileq sum_j_1+dots+j_m leq kfracsum_i=1^m (1- lambda^(i)_j_i)prod_i=1^mlambda^(i)_j_i nonumber \\ &leq& 2^m-1sum_j_1+dots+j_m leq ksum_i=1^mBig|1-frac1lambda^(i)_j_i Big|leq 2^m-1binomk+m-1m-1sum_i=1^msum_j=1^kBig|1-frac1lambda^(i)_j Big| nonumber \\ &leq & 2^m-1binomk+m-1m-1left(sum_i=1^m c(n_i,k)right)frac1r^2. Here, the coefficient 2^m-1 comes from the fact that lambda^(i)_j in [1/2,1], the coefficient binomk+m-1m-1 is the result of counting the tuple (j_1,dots,j_i-1,j_i+1,dots,j_m) such that sum_i=1^mj_i leq k, and the last inequality is based on Lemma~. In short, we can obtain the following inequality: \|K^-1f -f\|_X leq 2^m-1binomk+m-1m-1left(sum_i=1^m c(n_i,k)right)fracLambda(X,k) \|f\|_Xr^2, which proved and this completes the proof.

nodes.statement: For any k--truncated moment sequence y in M_k(X), there exists a probability measure kappa in P(X) corresponding to a moment sequence, whose projection onto the first s(n,k) coordinates is y. Moreover, because of Tchakaloff's theorem (see e.g.,), there exist at most N:=s(n,k) points \x_j: jin[N]\ subset mboxsupp(kappa) and corresponding positive weight \w_j: jin [N]\ satisfying sum_j=1^N w_j=1 such that for any f in R[x]_k, the integral of f over X with respect to kappa can be calculated as follows: int_Xf(x) dkappa(x) = sum_j=1^Nw_j f(x_j).

nodes.statement: Let Xsubset R^n be a compact set that is a product Pi_i=1^mX_i where each X_isubset R^n_i is either the unit ball B_n_i or standard simplex Delta_n_i. We assume that there exists R such that X subset B_R, and the inequality, R^2 -\|x\|^2 geq0, is included in the definition of X. For a fixed k=2l and r geq 2m(max\n_1,dots,n_m\+1)k+m, the Hausdorff distance d_k(T(X)_2r) admits the following upper bound: d_k(T(X)_2r) leq Gamma(X,k)dfrac2gamma(R,n,k)(r-m)^2. Here, the parameter gamma(R,n,k) is the radius of the ball centered at the origin that contains M_k(T(B_R)_2r), and it depends polynomially on n and k.

nodes.statement: Since both M_k(T(X)_2r) and M_k(X) are compact (this is elaborated in Remark~ below), we can let overliney in M_k(T(X)_2r) be a k-truncated pseudo-moment sequence such that d_k(T(X)_2r) := d( M_k(T(X)_2r),M_k(X)) = d(overliney, M_k(X)). Because X is compact and we have argued above by Tchakaloff's theorem that every k--truncated moment sequence is a convex combination of \v_k(x_1),ldots,v_k(x_N)\ with x_iinX for all iin [N] and N = s(n,k), we know that M_k(X) is a compact convex set. Hence, there exists the unique projection of overliney on M_k(X), denoted by Tildey, such that d_k(T(X)_2r)^2 = \|Tildey - overliney\|^2 = min\\|y - overliney\|^2\,:\, y in M_k(X)\. According to the first-order optimality condition, langle Tildey-overliney, y - Tildey rangle geq 0 for any y in M_k(X), and we obtain L(y):=langle Tildey-overliney, y - overliney rangle=langle Tildey-overliney, y - Tildey rangle +langle Tildey-overliney, Tildey - overlineyranglegeq d_k(T(X)_2r)^2 \;\; forall\; y in M_k(X). Hence, Tildey is also a minimizer of L(y) on M_k(X) with the minimum value d_k(T(X)_2r)^2. Consider the following problem undersety in M_k(X)min\ L(y) = sum_alpha in N^n_k(Tildey_alpha-overliney_alpha)y_alpha-langle Tildey-overliney, overliney rangle. This problem is actually the equivalent form of the following POP: min Bigl\\ f(x) = sum_alpha in N^n_k(Tildey_alpha-overliney_alpha)x^alpha-langle Tildey-overliney, overliney rangle \,:\, x in XBigr\. In addition, there exists a positive number gamma(R,n,k) such that for any 2r geq k, all the k-truncated pseudo-moment sequences of M_k(T(B_R)_2r) are contained in the ball centered at the origin with radius gamma(R,n,k) (see Remark~). Thus for any y in M_k(X)subset M_k(T(X)_2r) subset M_k(T(B_R)_2r), the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality implies that L(y)=langle Tildey-overliney, y - overliney rangle leq \|Tildey-overliney\| \| y - overliney\| leq d_k(T(X)_2r)(2 gamma(R,n,k)). Consider the problem with the conditions f_min = min_y in M_k(X) L(y)=d_k(T(X)_2r)^2 and f_max leq 2gamma(R,n,k) d_k(T(X)_2r). We apply the r-th level of the Schmüdgen-type moment hierarchy for the problem to get mlb(f,T(X))_r=undersety in M_k(T(X)_2r)min\ L(y) = langle Tildey-overliney, y - overliney rangle, whose error can be upper bounded by using Corollary~ under the degree condition r geq 2m(max\n_1,dots,n_m\+1)k+m as follows: f_min- mlb(f,T(X))_rleq Gamma(X,k)dfracf_max-f_min(r-m)^2 leq Gamma(X,k)dfrac2gamma(R,n,k) d_k(T(X)_2r)(r-m)^2. Since overliney in M_k(T(X)_2r), and L(overliney) =0, we get mlb(f,T(X))_r leq 0. From this, the inequality implies that d_k(T(X)_2r)^2 = f_min leq Gamma(X,k)dfrac2gamma(R,n,k) d_k(T(X)_2r)(r-m)^2 Rightarrow d_k(T(X)_2r) leq Gamma(X,k)dfrac2gamma(R,n,k) (r-m)^2. This completes the proof.

nodes.statement: From now on, we will frequently use the parameter gamma(R,n,k), where n denotes the dimension of variable x, k denotes the truncation order of the moment sequences, and R is the radius such that X subset B_R. Since we assume that the inequality R- \|x\|^2geq 0 is included in the description of X, therefore for any positive even integer k=2l, we always have M(T(X)_k) subset M(T(B_R)_k). Thus, gamma(R,n,k) can be used to bound the Euclidean norm of the pseudo-moment sequences in M(T(X)_k). The explicit expression of gamma(R,n,k) is given in the following lemma. [, Lemma 3] For k=2l, M(T(B_R)_k) is contained in the Euclidean ball centered at the origin with radius gamma(R,n,k):=sqrtbinomn+lnsum_i=0^lR^2i\,.

nodes.statement: Let X = prod_i=1^mX_i, where each X_i subset R^n_i is either the unit ball B_n_i or the standard simplex Delta_n_i. We choose the reference measure mu =otimes_i=1^mmu_i for X, where mu_i is the reference measure on X_i as in Table~. Let n =sum_i=1^m n_i. For any i in [m], let y^(i)=big(y^(i)_alpha^(i)in N^n_ibig) be the moment sequence with respect to mu_i. Then the moment sequence y=(y_alphain N^n) with respect to mu is defined as follows: for any alpha= (alpha^(1),dots,alpha^(m)) in N^n with alpha^(i) in N^n_i\; forall i in [m], the alpha-component of y is defined by y_alpha= prod_i=1^m y^(i)_alpha^(i). In addition, for a given f(x)in R[x] of degree k, consider the POP f_min := min_x in Xf(x). Then for any integer r > 2(max\n_1,ldots,n_m\+1)k, the following inequality holds: ub(f,T(X))_mr-f_min leq binomk+m-1m-1left(sum_i=1^m c(n_i,k)right)fracLambda(X,k)\|f\|_Xr^2. Consequently, the convergence rate of the Schm\"udgen-type hierarchy of upper-bounds over the product of unit balls and standard simplexes is O(1/r^2).

For a fixed positive integer r, let x^* be one of the minimizers of f over X, whose existence is due to the compactness of X. We recall the perturbed CD kernel C_2r[X,mu,lambda] from Theorem~ and set sigma(x) = C_2r[X,mu,lambda](x,x^*). In the proof of Theorem~, we have pointed out that sigma(x):= C_2r[X,mu,lambda](x,x^*)in T(X)_2mr. Whence, we have f_min leq ub(f,T(X))_mr leq int_Xf(x)sigma(x)dmu(x)=C_2r[X,mu,lambda]f(x^*). Note that f(x) admits the following decomposition f(x) = sum_j_1+dots+j_m leq kf_j_1,dots,j_m(x), f_j_1,dots,j_m in S_j_1,dots,j_m\ forall j_1+dots+j_m leq k. Thus, the image of f under C_2r[X,mu,lambda] is C_2r[X,mu,lambda]f(x) = sum_j_1+dots+j_m leq k Big(prod_i=1^mlambda^(i)_j_iBig) f_j_1,dots,j_m(x). We assume that the inequality g_0(x) = R^2 -\|x\|^2 geq 0 is added to the description of X. For any k = 2l inN and r in N such that kgeq 4d and r geq 2s(max\n_1,dots,n_s\+1)k+s, where d is defined in , the Hausdorff distance d_k(R(X)_2r) := d(M_k(R(X)_2r),M_k(X)) admits an upper bound as follows: d_k(R(X)_2r) leq dfrac2gamma(R,n,k)Gamma(Y,k)(r-s)^2+ cL(R,k)left(dfrac2gamma(R,n,k)\, Gamma(Y,k)(r-s)^2right)^L/2 left(sum_i=1^p\|h_i^2\|_1right)^L/2. First, we conduct two consecutive projections as follows: since M_k(X) subset M_k(Y), we first project y onto M_k(Y) and denote its projection by overliney. By Tchakaloff's theorem, overliney can be written as a convex combination of some v_k(overlinex_j)'s with points \overlinex_j : jin[N]\ subset Y. We continue projecting overlinex_j onto X to define a new moment sequence widetildey in M_k(X). These projections are demonstrated in Figure~ and elaborated in the later part of the proof. Then we can upper bound the distance of y to M_k(X) by the triangle inequality: d(y,M_k(X)) \;leq\; \|y - widetildey\| \;leq\; \|y-overliney\| + \|overliney-widetildey\|. The idea of upper-bounding d(y,M_k(X)) by \|y-overliney\| and \|overliney-widetildey\| is based on the fact that we already have Theorem~ and the Łojasiewicz inequality~ as tools to evaluate these terms, which is elaborated next. Therefore, we can rewrite the equalities of the Riesz functional associated with y and overliney as follows: ell_y(h_i^2) = langle h_i^2, y rangle= 0, mboxand ell_overliney(h_i^2) =langle h_i^2, overliney rangle= sum_j=1^N w_j langle h_i^2,v_k(overlinex_j)rangle = sum_j=1^N w_j h_i^2(overlinex_j), where h_i^2 denotes the vector of coefficients of h_i^2(x). Let x_jinX be the projection of overlinex_jinY onto X for all j in [N]. We define widetildey \;=\; sum_j=1^N w_jv_k(x_j) \;in M_k(X). Indeed, we can write K^2 - u_j^2= (K-u_j)(K+u_j)= Bigl(K-sum_l=1^m u_l +sum_l neq ju_lBigr)(K+u_j) \\ = KBigl(K-sum_l=1^m u_lBigr)+u_jBigl(K-sum_l=1^m u_lBigr) + K sum_lneq j u_l + sum_lneq j u_l u_j in Tbig((B_R times Delta_K^m)_2rbig) forall j in [m]. This implies that we can write widehatp_0 as a sum of elements of T(B_R times Delta_K^m)_2r of degree at most 2. In other words, for any product polynomial q of p_0,\; p_j,\; j in [m+1] with degree at most 2t and y in M(T(B_R times Delta_K^m)_2r), we have &&widehatp_0q = p_0q+sum_j=1^mBiggl[KBigl(K-sum_l=1^m u_lBigr)+u_jBigl(K-sum_l=1^m u_lBigr) + K sum_l neq ju_l + sum_lneq ju_lu_j Bigr]q \\ &Rightarrow&\; M_r-t-1(widehatp_0qy) = M_r-t-1(p_0qy)+sum_j=1^mKM_r-t-1Biggl(Bigl(K-sum_l=1^m u_lBigr)qyBiggr)\\ && +M_r-t-1Biggl(u_jBigl(K-sum_l=1^m u_lBigr)qyBiggr) +sum_l neq j K M_r-t-1 (u_l qy) + sum_lneq j M_r-t-1Biggl(u_l u_jqyBiggr) succeq 0. If we add widehatp_0(z) geq 0 into the description of B_R times Delta_K^m, the new constraint added to M(T(B_R times Delta_K^m)_2r) then take the form of M_r-t-1(widehatp_0qy) succeq 0. However, as we have shown above, the constraint is already satisfied without adding widehatp_0(z) geq 0. Thus, adding it does not change M(T(B_R times Delta_K^m)_2r). Furthermore, applying Lemma~ gives us that M_k(T(B_R times Delta_K^m)_2r) is a compact set contained in the Euclidean ball centered at the origin with radius gamma(n+m,R+mK^2,k). Applying Theorem~ for the product of two simple sets, we obtain that d_k(T(B_R times Delta_K^m)_2r) leq Gamma(B_R times Delta_K^m,k)dfrac2gamma(n+m,R+mK^2,k)(r-2)^2, which is the upper bound we desire. Notice that varphi(X) subset B_R times Delta_K^m, and both M_k(T(varphi(X))_2r) and M_k(R(varphi(X))_2r) are closed subsets of M_k(T(B_R times Delta_K^m)_2r). Hence, we can claim that these sets are also compact.

We show that the constraint $\widehat{p}_0(\mathbf{z}) :=R+ mK^2 - \|\mathbf{x}\|^2 - \sum_{j=1}^m u_j^2 \geq 0$ can be added to the description of $\mathbb{B}_R \times \Delta_K^m$ without changing $\mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{T}(\mathbb{B}_R \times \Delta_K^m)_{2r})$.
     Indeed, we can write
     \begin{multline*}
         K^2 - u_j^2= (K-u_j)(K+u_j)= \Bigl(K-\sum_{l=1}^m u_l +\sum_{l \neq j}u_l\Bigr)(K+u_j)
         \\
         = K\Bigl(K-\sum_{l=1}^m u_l\Bigr)+u_j\Bigl(K-\sum_{l=1}^m u_l\Bigr) 
         + K \sum_{l\neq j} u_l + \sum_{l\neq j} u_l u_j \in 
         
         \mathcal{T}\big((\mathbb{B}_R \times \Delta_K^m)_{2r}\big)
         \quad \forall j \in [m].
     \end{multline*}
     This implies that we can write $\widehat{p}_0$ as a sum of elements of $\mathcal{T}(\mathbb{B}_R \times \Delta_K^m)_{2r}$ of degree at most $2$. In other words, for any product polynomial $q$ of $p_0,\; p_j,\; j \in [m+1]$ with degree at most $2t$ and $\mathit{y} \in \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{T}(\mathbb{B}_R \times \Delta_K^m)_{2r})$, we have 
     \begin{eqnarray*}
         &&\widehat{p}_0q = p_0q+\sum_{j=1}^m\Biggl[K\Bigl(K-\sum_{l=1}^m  
         u_l\Bigr)+u_j\Bigl(K-\sum_{l=1}^m u_l\Bigr) 
         + K \sum_{l \neq j}u_l
         + \sum_{l\neq j}u_lu_j
         \Bigr]q
         \\
         &\Rightarrow&\; \mathbf{M}_{r-t-1}(\widehat{p}_0q\mathit{y})
         = \mathbf{M}_{r-t-1}(p_0q\mathit{y})+\sum_{j=1}^mK\mathbf{M}_{r-t-1}\Biggl(\Bigl(K-\sum_{l=1}^m
         u_l\Bigr)q\mathit{y}\Biggr)\\
         &&\qquad +\mathbf{M}_{r-t-1}\Biggl(u_j\Bigl(K-\sum_{l=1}^m u_l\Bigr)q\mathit{y}\Biggr) +\sum_{l \neq j} K \mathbf{M}_{r-t-1} (u_l qy) 
         + \sum_{l\neq j} \mathbf{M}_{r-t-1}\Biggl(u_l u_jq\mathit{y}\Biggr) \succeq 0.
     \end{eqnarray*}
     If we add $\widehat{p}_0(\mathbf{z}) \geq 0$ into the description of $\mathbb{B}_R \times \Delta_K^m$, the new constraint added to $\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{T}(\mathbb{B}_R \times \Delta_K^m)_{2r})$
     
     then take the form of 
     \begin{equation*}
         \mathbf{M}_{r-t-1}(\widehat{p}_0q\mathit{y}) \succeq 0.
     \end{equation*}
     However, as we have shown above, the constraint is already satisfied without adding $\widehat{p}_0(\mathbf{z}) \geq 0$. Thus, adding it does not change 
     $\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{T}(\mathbb{B}_R \times \Delta_K^m)_{2r})$. Furthermore, applying Lemma~\ref{lemm: radius of preordering} gives us that $\mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{T}(\mathbb{B}_R \times \Delta_K^m)_{2r})$ is a compact set contained in the Euclidean ball centered at the origin with radius $\gamma(n+m,R+mK^2,k)$. Applying Theorem~\ref{thm: error on product of simple sets} for the product of two simple sets, we obtain that
     \begin{equation*}
         \mathbf{d}_k(\mathcal{T}(\mathbb{B}_R \times \Delta_K^m)_{2r}) \leq \Gamma(\mathbb{B}_R \times \Delta_K^m,k)\dfrac{2\gamma(n+m,R+mK^2,k)}{(r-2)^2},
     \end{equation*}
     which is the upper bound we desire. 
 
  Notice that $\varphi(\mathcal{X}) \subset \mathbb{B}_R \times \Delta_K^m$, and both $\mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{T}(\varphi(\mathcal{X}))_{2r})$ and $\mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{R}(\varphi(\mathcal{X}))_{2r})$ are closed subsets of $\mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{T}(\mathbb{B}_R \times \Delta_K^m)_{2r})$. Hence, we can claim that these sets are also compact.

    For the case $k \leq 2r$, since $\mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{T}(\mathbb{B}_R)_{2r})$ 
    
    is the first $s(n,k)$--coordinate 
    
    projection of $\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{T}(\mathbb{B}_R)_{2r})$, 
    
    we obtain that $\psi_k(\mathit{y}) \in \mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{T}(\mathbb{B}_R)_{2r})$.

nodes.statement: Let y in M_k(R(X)_2r) be an arbitrary truncated pseudo-moment sequence. We proceed to bound the distance from y to M_k(X) by finding an appropriate point widetildey in M_k(X) and a point overliney in M_k(B_R) such that d(y,M_k(X)) leq \|y- widetildey\| leq \|y- overliney\| + \|overliney- widetildey\|. The idea of finding overliney and widetildey is through lifting M_k(X) to M(T(varphi(X))_2r), where varphi(X) is the intersection of a real variety and the product B_R times Delta_K^m of simple sets. We first find the corresponding points overliney' and widetildey' in the lifted spaces and then obtain the desired points overliney and widetildey by the projection psi_k defined as in Lemma~. We can conduct the proof as in Theorem~. The detail is elaborated below. item Since y in M_k(R(X)_2r), there exists widehaty in M(R(X)_2r) such that y = pi_k(widehaty). Lemma~ implies that widehaty^varphi in M(T(varphi(X))_2t). Let overliney^prime in M_2t(B_R times Delta_K^m) be the projection of widehaty^varphi onto M_2t(B_R times Delta_K^m). We set overliney= psi_k(pi_k(overliney^prime)) in M_k(B_R) (by Lemma~). item By Tchakaloff's theorem, there exist at most N = s(n+m,2t) points \overlinez_1,dots,overlinez_N\ subset B_R times Delta_K^m and positive weights \w_s : sin [N]\ satisfying that sum_s=1^Nw_s =1 and overliney^prime = sum_s=1^N w_s v_2t(overlinez_s). For any s in [N], overlinez_s = (overlinex_s, overlineu_s1,dots,overlineu_sm), we set x_s to be the projection of overlinex_s onto X. Then we define widetildey^prime &=&sum_s=1^Nw_s v_2tbig( (x_s,g_1(x_s),dots,g_m(x_s))big)in M_2t(varphi(X)), \\ widetildey &=& psi_k(pi_k(widetildey^prime))= sum_s=1^Nw_s v_k(x_s) in M_k(X). Figure~ illustrates our idea. After defining overliney and widetildey, we evaluate each term in . Evaluating \|y -overliney\|: We apply Lemma~ to d_k(T(B_R times Delta_K^m)_2t) under the degree condition t geq 4(max\n,m\+1)k+2 for a product of two simple sets to obtain that \|y - overliney\| = \|psi_k(pi_k(widehaty^varphi)) - psi_k(pi_k(overliney^prime))\| leq \|pi_k(widehaty^varphi)- pi_k(overliney^prime)\| \\ \;leq\; d_k(T(B_R times Delta_K^m)_2t) \;leq\; dfracGamma(B_R times Delta_K^m,k)2gamma(n+m,R+mK^2,k)(t-2)^2 =: varepsilon. Evaluating \|overliney-widetildey\|: We use the same argument as in the proof of Theorem~ to derive the following inequality: sum_s=1^N w_s maxleft\ |h_i(overlinex_s)|:\ i in [p]right\ leq varepsilon^1/2 sum_i=1^p \|h_i\|_1. For j in [m], we consider q_j(z) = (g_j(x)-u_j)^2. Then we have ell_widehaty^varphi(q_j) = ell_y((g_j(x)-g_j(x))^2) =0, mboxand \|q_j\|_1leq (1+\|g_j\|_1)^2. Note that deg(q_j) leq 4d leq k. Next, using the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality and the fact that overlineu_s=(overlineu_s1,ldots,overlineu_sm) geq 0\; forall\; sin [N], we have &sum_s=1^Nw_sq_j(overlinez_s) = sum_s=1^Nw_sq_j(overlinez_s)-ell_widehaty^varphi(q_j) = leftlangle q_j,overliney^prime - widehaty^varphi rightrangle leq varepsilon \|q_j\|_1 mbox(by ) \\ Rightarrow & sum_s=1^N w_s(g_j(overlinex_s)-overlineu_sj)^2 leq varepsilon \|q_j\|_1 Rightarrow sum_s=1^Nw_s max \0, -g_j(overlinex_s)\^2 leq varepsilon \|q_j\|_1\\ Rightarrow & sum_s=1^N w_smax \0, -g_j(overlinex_s)\ leq left( sum_s=1^Nw_sright)^1/2left( sum_s=1^Nw_s max \0, -g_j(overlinex_s)\^2right)^1/2 leq varepsilon^1/2(1+\|g_j\|_1)\\ Rightarrow & sum_s=1^Nw_s max left\-g_j(overlinex_s),|h_i(overlinex_s)|:\ iin [p],\ jin [m]right\leq varepsilon^1/2left(m+sum_j=1^m\|g_j\|_1+sum_i=1^p\|h_i\|_1right). Furthermore, the Łojasiewicz inequality~ implies that \|x_s -overlinex_s\| = d(overlinex_s,X) leq cmax left\-g_j(overlinex_s),|h_i(overlinex_s)|:\ iin [p],\ jin [m]right\^L. Let L(R,k)>0 be the Lipschitz number of v_k(x) on the ball B_R. Then it directly leads to the inequality: \|v_k(x_s) - v_k(overlinex_s)\| leq L(R,k) \|x_s -overlinex_s\| leq cL(R,k) max left\-g_j(overlinex_s),|h_i(overlinex_s)|:\ iin [p],\ jin [m]right\^L. Hence, we obtain that \|overliney-widetildey \| &=& left\|sum_s=1^N w_sv_k(overlinex_s) - sum_s=1^N w_sv_k(x_s)right\| \\ &leq& cL(R,k)sum_s=1^N w_smax left\-g_j(overlinex_s),|h_i(overlinex_s)|:\ iin [p],\ jin [m]right\^L. Recall that L leq 1, applying Jensen's inequality gives us the following inequality: &sum_s=1^N w_smax left\-g_j(overlinex_s),|h_i(overlinex_s)|:\ iin [p],\ jin [m]right\^Lnonumber\\ leq &\ left(sum_s=1^N w_smax left\-g_j(overlinex_s),|h_i(overlinex_s)|:\ iin [p],\ jin [m]right\right)^Lnonumber\\ Rightarrow &\ sum_s=1^N w_smax left\-g_j(overlinex_s),|h_i(overlinex_s)|:\ iin [p],\ jin [m]right\^L leqvarepsilon^L/2left(m+sum_j=1^m\|g_j\|_1+sum_i=1^p\|h_i\|_1right)^Lnonumber\\ Rightarrow&\ \|overliney-widetildey \| leq cL(R,k)varepsilon^L/2left(m+sum_j=1^m\|g_j\|_1+sum_i=1^p\|h_i\|_1right)^L. We substitute and back to to obtain that &d(y,M_k(X)) leq varepsilon+cL(R,k) varepsilon^L/2left(m+sum_j=1^m\|g_j\|_1+sum_i=1^p\|h_i\|_1right)^L forall y in M_k(R(X)_2r) \\ Rightarrow& \ d_k(R(X)_2r) leq varepsilon+cL(R,k) varepsilon^L/2left(m+sum_j=1^m\|g_j\|_1+sum_i=1^p\|h_i\|_1right)^L. By the definition t, we have t geq fracr-2d2d. Hence, we obtain that d_k(R(X)_2r) leq Gamma(B_R times Delta_K^m,k)2gamma(n+m,R+mK^2,k)dfrac(2d)^2(r-4d)^2 \\ +fraccL(R,k)(2d)^L(r-4d)^L [Gamma(B_R times Delta_K^m,k)2gamma(n+m,R+mK^2,k)]^L/2 left(m+sum_j=1^m\|g_j\|_1+sum_i=1^p\|h_i\|_1right)^L. This completes the proof.

For x in Omega backslash mboxargmin(g), g(x) > 0. Thus, the set A(x) of active indices at x, defined as A(x) = \i in [m]:\ g(x) = g_i(x)\ neq emptyset. Additionally, we can combine it with to obtain the subdifferential of the maximum of differentiable functions as partial^Fg(x) = partial^Lg(x) = partial g(x) = conv\nabla g_i(x)\; :\; i in A(x)\. For any w in partial g(x), we set w = sum_i in A(x) w_inabla g_i(x) where 0 leq w_i leq 1 for all i in A(x) and sum_i in A(x)w_i =1. Observe that inf_R^n f = inf_Omega g =0, and argmin\ f = X. For any widehatx in Omega, we construct a sequence (x_k)_k in N as follows: x_0 =widehatx, and x_k+1 in undersetx in R^nargmin f(x) + dfrac12\|x-x_k\|^2, S_k+1 = \x in R^n:\ f(x) leq f(x_k+1)\. We use the chain rule to obtain that partial(varphi circ f)(x) subset varphi'(f(x))partial f(x) Rightarrow 1 leq \|v\| \;\; forall v in partial(varphi circ f)(x), forall\; xin Omega. The above result can be combined with the condition of to show that the limiting slope of f at x (see e.g., ), denoted by left|overlinenabla f(x)right|, satisfies that left|overlinenabla f(x)right| = d(0, partial f(x)) = inf left\\|v\|,\ v in partial f(x) right\ geq 1 \ forall\; x in Omega. \label{thm: error and rate under the strong convexity}
            Let $\mathcal{X} \subset \interior{\Omega}$ be either a strongly convex semi-algebraic set as in Assumption \ref{assumption: convexisty} or the violating function $g$ satisfies the Polyak-Łojasiewicz condition, where $\interior{\Omega}$ is 
            the interior of the convex set $\Omega$. Then the error for the set of truncated pseudo-moment sequences and the convergence rate of the Schm\"udgen-type moment-SOS hierarchy
            $\mathcal{M}_k(\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{X})_{2r})$ is $\mathrm{O}(1/\sqrt{r})$.

nodes.statement: We recall that under either the strong convexity condition in Assumption or the Polyak-Łojasiewicz condition, the Łojasiewicz exponent of X on Omega is 1/2. To apply Theorem~ with L = 1/2, it is necessary to show that the Łojasiewicz exponent of X on B_R is also 1/2 for some radius R such that X subset B_R. This relies on the containment of X within the interior of Omega, which allows the Łojasiewicz exponent of 1/2 to be extended to B_R. This concept is illustrated in Figure~. \\ filldraw[fill=gray!10, draw=black] (0,0) circle (2.5cm); filldraw[fill=white!10, draw=black] (0,0) ellipse (2cm and 1.5cm); filldraw[fill=gray!10, draw=black] (0,0) ellipse (1.3cm and 0.7cm); draw[->, thick] (-1.9,0) -- (-1.4,0); draw[->, thick] (1.9,0) -- (1.4,0); draw[->, thick] (-1.1,-1.1) -- (-0.7,-0.7); draw[->, thick] (-1.1,1.1) -- (-0.7,0.7); draw[->, thick] (1.1,1.1) -- (0.7,0.7); draw[->, thick] (1.1,-1.1) -- (0.7,-0.7); draw[->, thick] (0,-1.3) -- (0,-0.8); node at (0,0) X; node at (0,1) Omega; node at (0,2) B_R; captionProof of Theorem~. Note that from Lemmas and , there exist the the Łojasiewicz exponent 1/2 and constant c such that d(x,X) leq c g(x)^1/2 forall\; x in Omega. Since X subset interiorOmega, g(x) is continuous on B_R, and X = g^-1(0), we obtain that min_x in B_R backslash interiorOmegafraccg(x)^1/2d(x,X) > 0, eta := min left\ 1,min_x in B_R backslash interiorOmegafraccg(x)^1/2d(x,X)right\ > 0. Then we can construct a version of the Łojasiewicz inequality of X over B_R as follows: &d(x,X) leq c g(x)^1/2 leq fracceta g(x)^1/2 forall\; x in Omega, d(x,X) leq fracceta g(x)^1/2 forall\; x in B_Rbackslash interiorOmega\\ Rightarrow \;& d(x,X) leq fracceta g(x)^1/2 forall \; x in B_R. This implies that the Łojasiewicz exponent of X on B_R is 1/2, which is what we desire.

nodes.statement: Let A be an m times n matrix, and beta be the least number such that for each non-singular sub-matrix B of A, all entries of B^-1 are at most beta in absolute value. Consider the polyhedron P defined by a system of linear inequalities Ax^prime leq b^prime. Then for each b^0 in R^m and x^0 in R^n such that Ax^0 leq b^0, there exists x^prime in R^n satisfying &Ax^prime leq b^prime, mboxand \|x^0-x^prime\|_infty leq nbeta \|b^0-b^prime\|_infty. Consequently, the Łojasiewicz exponent of P is 1. Here, \|cdot\|_infty denotes the infinity norm of a vector.

nodes.statement: We first proceed as in the proof of Theorem~. Let y in M_k(T(S_R^n-1)_2r). Then y in M_k(T(B_R)_2r), and there exists the projection overliney of y onto M_k(B_R) such that \|y -overliney\| \;leq\; frac2gamma(R,n,k) Gamma(B_R,k)r^2=: varepsilon. Moreover, there exists N leq s(n,k) points \overlinex_s:\; sin[N]\ in B_R and positive weight \w_s:\; sin [N]\ with sum_s=1^Nw_s =1 satisfying that overliney= sum_s=1^Nw_sv_k(overlinex_s). Applying the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality to left|ell_y(R^2-\|x\|^2)-ell_overliney(R^2-\|x\|^2)right|, we obtain the following: &left|ell_y(R^2-\|x\|^2)-ell_overliney(R^2-\|x\|^2)right| leq sum_i=1^n |y_2e_i - overliney_2e_i| leq sqrtn\|y-overliney\| \\ Rightarrow\;& left|ell_overliney(R^2-\|x\|^2) right| leq sqrtnvarepsilon (since ell_y(R^2 - \|x\|^2) = 0)\\ Rightarrow\;& sum_s=1^Nw_s(R^2-\|overlinex_s\|^2) leq sqrtnvarepsilon. Define widetildex_s = R\,overlinex_s/\|overlinex_s\| in S_R^n-1 to be the projection of overlinex_s onto S_R^n-1. Then we can bound the distance between overlinex_s and widetildex_s as follows: \|widetildex_s-overlinex_s\| = left\|overlinex_sleft(fracR\|overlinex_s\|-1 right)right\|= R-\|overlinex_s\| leq frac(R+\|overlinex_s\|)(R-\|overlinex_s\|)R= fracR^2-\|overlinex_s\|^2R. We set widetildey= sum_s=1^Nw_sv_k(widetildex_s). Since widetildex_s in S_R^n-1\; forall s in [N], widetildey in M_k(S_R^n-1). Moreover, let L(R,k) be the Lipschitz number of v_k(x) on the ball B_R. Then we can perform the following evaluation on the distance between overliney and widetildey as follows: &\|overliney-widetildey\| leq sum_s=1^Nw_s\|v_k(overlinex_s)-v_k(widetildex_s)\| leq sum_s=1^Nw_sL(R,k)\|overlinex_s-widetildex_s\|\\ leq\; & sum_s=1^Nw_sL(R,k)fracR^2-\|overlinex_s\|^2R = fracL(R,k)Rsum_s=1^Nw_s(R^2-\|overlinex_s\|^2) leq fracsqrtnL(R,k)Rvarepsilon. Hence, we can bound the distance from y to M_k(S_R^n-1) as d_k(T(S_R^n-1)_2r) leq \|y -widetildey\| leq \|y - overliney\| + \| overliney-widetildey\| leq varepsilonleft(1+ fracsqrtnL(R,k)R right). In conclusion, we obtain the desired bound. This completes the proof.

nodes.statement: Consider the domain X = \x in R^n:\; g_i(x) geq 0,\; iin [m] \. For x in X, let I(x) be the set of active indices (the index i is said to be active if g_i(x) = 0). We say that the Constraint Qualification Condition (CQC) holds at x if \ nabla g_i(x):\; i in I(x)\ are linearly independent. We say that X satisfy the CQC if the CQC holds at every point of X. In this case, the Łojasiewicz exponent is equal to 1.

nodes.statement: Let X be a product of simple sets defined by X := \ x in R^n:\ g_j(x) geq 0\ forall j in [m]\. Let k= 2l be a positive even integer, A be an invertible matrix in R^ntimes n. Then the image of X via A remains a basic semi-algebraic set defined by A(X) = \x in R^n:\ g_j(A^-1x) geq 0\ forall j in [m]\. We have the following upper bound on the error of truncated pseudo-moment sequences: d_k(T(A(X)))_r leq Gamma(A(X),k)dfracgamma(R,n,k)r^2, where Gamma(A(X)),k) is a polynomial in the dimension n, the norm of A and k. The result also holds true for Q(A(X))_2r and R(A(X))_2r.

nodes.statement: Theorem~ can be proved similarly as in Theorem~ when X is a product of simple sets by constructing a push-forward measure on A(X). In particular, let mu be the measure on X used in the proof of Theorem~. We consider the push-forward measure mu circ A^-1, and note that A is invertible. Then the CD kernel on A(X) can be reconstructed, for which the same arguments as in the proof of Theorem~ remain valid. However, we propose here another proof for a general set X that also explains how a pseudo-moment sequence is transformed under the action of an invertible linear transformation on the domain.
nodes.raw_latex:
Theorem~\ref{thm: error on image}  can be proved similarly as in Theorem~\ref{thm: error on product of simple sets} when $\mathcal{X}$ is a product of simple sets by constructing a push-forward measure on 
        $A(\mathcal{X})$. In particular, let $\mu $ be the measure on $\mathcal{X}$ used in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm: error on product of simple sets}. We consider the push-forward measure $\mu \circ A^{-1}$, and note that $A$ is invertible. Then the CD kernel on $A(\mathcal{X})$ can be reconstructed, for which the same arguments as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm: error on product of simple sets} remain valid. However, we propose here another proof for a general set $\mathcal{X}$ that also explains how a pseudo-moment sequence is transformed under the action of an invertible linear transformation on the domain.

Then the CD kernel on A(X) can be reconstructed, for which the same arguments as in the proof of Theorem~ remain valid. However, we propose here another proof for a general set X that also explains how a pseudo-moment sequence is transformed under the action of an invertible linear transformation on the domain.
